_doc: Plain-language scoreboard for the C10 problem (made-up multi-word names), shown by code/apps/dashboard/dashboard_report.py. The program session updates it at every result and close-out: add a results row, refresh current/queue, rewrite the brief in plain words. Scores are held-out reworded questions answered exactly right, out of 72. Full detail lives in CORPUS; this file only points there.
brief: We are trying to teach the model made-up names (like a project codename) so it can recall them when a question is worded differently. Ordinary facts already work (about 69 of 72); made-up two-word names do not: the usual method gets about 12 of 72, our best write method about 40, and the goal is 61. Training the same small part of the model reaches 70 of 72, so that part is big enough, but only with side effects. ASTRA, which writes every word of the answer at once, got 14 of 72 against 12 and did not fit its targets, so it is closed. The offline math lab could not predict real results well enough and was stopped. Now: a check of the math behind earlier writes (NEW-1) and the step-7 setup.

current.what: NEW-1 (math check of earlier writes): its first run stopped on a setup check; the saved data reproduces exactly, and a second short check you approved is being built (CPU only).
Step 7 (solve the weight change directly): stopped at calibration; its next check waits on a storage decision now that Google Drive is ready.

results.name: Step 4: let each fact pick its own depth
results.verdict: No: one more right answer than the usual method, and putting every fact at one fixed depth did just as well; not taken forward

results.name: Step 5: ceiling test, repeat run (training, not a write)
results.verdict: Stopped before the official reading: the new seed scored 71 of 72 and the same-seed retrain 70 of 72 (identical to the first round), but a rounding bug in the final self-check blocked the reading; no conclusion yet, needs your ruling

results.name: Step 5: ceiling test, official reading (training, not a write)
results.verdict: Training this small part of the model can recall made-up two-word names at 70 to 71 of 72, so its size is not the wall; but it got there with side effects (other facts disturbed, general-knowledge loss on one run), so a clean ceiling is not shown

results.name: Step 6: two ways to prepare the answer before writing it
results.verdict: No: re-weighting the answer's words gave 17 of 72 against 12, too small to count; the other idea made the ordinary control facts worse (64 and 65 of 72, below 68), so its score is not read, and its own answer-preparation step also missed its fit check (3 of 24 against 22); neither is taken forward

results.name: Math lab: predict a write's result offline
results.verdict: Stopped: its offline predictions did not match the real runs closely enough to trust, so it is not used to rank ideas

results.name: ASTRA: write every word of the answer at once
results.verdict: No: two more right answers than the usual method, but it did not fit its targets, changed too much of the model and disturbed unrelated facts; closed under the current approval
